input.content: Pattern: Independent-release compatibility break — a new client hard-requires a response field the currently-released provider does not yet emit. In enhanced-settings Task 1, client.save_settings added `if response.get("applied") is not True: raise RuntimeError`, but the released provider (provider/settings.py update_settings) returns only `{"ok": True}`. Result: every ordinary save against the supported provider raises, violating the design's explicit "ordinary saves must continue to work with the supported provider" and "independently releasable main" requirements. The provider-side receipt was a separate pending task in another repo. Lesson: when adding a new field to a request/response protocol across independently-released components, the consumer must tolerate the absence of the field until the producer ships (treat missing as backward-compatible / gate the enforcement), otherwise the increment is not independently releasable. Also watch for tests mutated to inject the new field (applied: True) which mask the break by never exercising the old-provider response shape.
